entries.title: Online co-op
items: Co-op is here: fly any mission with up to three friends. Open Co-op from the title screen or the hangar menu, host a room, and send the four-letter code, the link or the QR code.
Friends can join in the middle of a mission and land right beside you. If someone's connection drops, a bot flies their frame until they're back (up to 90 seconds).
Everyone brings their own frame and keeps their own loot, rolled at their own rank. The pay is never split: everyone gets all of it.
Enemies get tougher and there are more of them for each extra frame in the team.
Bots: fill empty seats with bot pilots, or bring up to three of them on a solo mission from the briefing. They stick with you, fight, revive you and plant charges.
When a teammate goes down, stand next to them: a ring fills, and they're back up. Press C (d-pad up) to ping a spot or an enemy for the team.
Rooms can be Invite only or Public; public rooms show up under Find a game. The host can remove someone, and everyone else can vote to.
Pick your callsign on the Co-op screen; teammates see it over your frame.
Fixed: the header bar on the contracts board was squashed so its Back button overlapped the page.
Once a mission's job is done, a green arrow at the edge of the screen points to the dropship (with how far it is), and a beam marks the pad.
Fixed: Report a bug could get stuck on "Sending…". It now always finishes, and a report that can't be sent waits on your device and goes later.

entries.title: The hangar and the city campaign
items: The hangar is open: walk your frame around it and step into a bay to use it. There's an assembly bay, a parts dealer, a workshop, a paint bay, a test range and the launch pad.

Every part you pick up is now a real part with a rarity (Common to Experimental) and bonus lines. Grade A and S missions give crates with more parts, materials, and sometimes firmware chips or secret recipes.

Assembly bay: change any part or weapon, and see how each swap changes your armour, speed, energy and the rest before you fit it. Save up to eight builds. All four makers' starter frames are already yours.
Firmware chips go in your CPU: more crit chance, faster locks, more energy, or a two-handed weapon held in one arm.
Workshop: build parts you've seen, re-roll a bonus, raise a part's rarity, burn chips, or scrap parts you don't need. Secret recipes for odd weapons turn up as schematics in crates.
Paint bay: 16 paint schemes (more unlock as your rank rises) or your own colours, kept per build.
Test range: try your build on target dummies, with damage per second on screen.
Pilot rank: missions earn experience. Higher ranks bring better parts to the dealer and unlock recipes.

The campaign: free the city of Larkspur one district at a time. The map lights back up as you go. Four new story missions: stop a truck convoy, plant charges on relay masts, escort evacuation trucks, and a drop from orbit where you steer your own landing.
A rival ace: Sawtooth, a Halden-Voss pilot in her own frame, who boosts, dodges and overheats just like you. Two more rival pilots are waiting later in the campaign.

The first boss: the Broodmother. Burst her egg sacs and break her claws to open her armoured head. Her claw sweeps, charges and spit always show on the ground before they land. Broken parts drop chitin, a new boss material.
Contracts: new jobs appear in every district you can reach, refreshed after each mission: clear-outs, nest burns, demolition, hunts, sabotage, data-core recovery, convoy raids and escorts.
Maker licences: contracts earn a maker's trust. Licences put more of their parts on the dealer's shelves, even above your rank, at a discount.
Signed in, your pilot is saved to your account. If two devices disagree, you choose which save to keep, and the other is kept so you can swap back from Settings.

entries.title: Overdrive Frame is here
items: Pick one of four makers' frames and drop into a neon city to take contracts: clear a swarm-filled district, burn a rival company's tank farms, or hold the line while the last evacuation trains leave.
Your frame boosts, quick-boosts sideways, jumps onto rooftops and hovers. Boosting and firing use energy and build heat, so watch the two arcs around your mech.
Hundreds of enemies at once: swarms that pour in along the streets, leapers, acid spitters and armoured brutes you have to get behind, plus troopers, tanks, rocket artillery and gunships.
Buildings break apart as they take damage, burn, and collapse onto whatever is next to them. Fuel tanks blow up.
Every mission ends with a grade from S to D that sets your pay. Losing never costs your frame; you keep what you picked up.
